paper_metadata.title: Enhanced high temperature strength in near-eutectic Al-8Ce alloy through Y addition by gravity casting
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: In this study, the heat resistant Al -8Ce-xY (x ¼ 0, 1, 2, and 3) alloys as designed and fabricated by gravity casting.
The microstructure and mechanical properties of Al e8Ce-xY (x ¼ 0, 1, 2, and 3) alloys containing eutectic colonies and Al matrices were investigated.
The experimental Al -8Ce-xY (x ¼ 0, 1, 2 and 3) alloys were synthesised using permanent mould casting with a steel crucible using pure commercial Al and Al-20Ce and Al-5Y master alloys.

First, pure bulk Al was melted in a resistance furnace at 750 °C. The Al-20Ce and Al-5Y master alloys were dried at 200 °C for 10 h and were then added to the melt. Subsequently, the melt was refined and degassed at 750 °C to remove dross/oxides from the melt surface. Finally, the temperature was decreased to 720 °C, and the melt was poured into a permanent metal mould to obtain flat cast ingots.

Yttrium additions produced the eutectic lamellar Al 11(Ce,Y)3 phase whose volume fraction increased from 10.45 to 19.15% with increasing Y additions from 0 to 3%.
The second phase strengthening from eutectic Al11(Ce,Y)3 phase is the main strengthening mechanism for Al e8Ce-xY alloys.

The yield and tensile strength of the Ale8Ce-xY alloys at room temperature increased from 65.1 to 72.5 MPa and from 117.5 to 142.7 MPa, respectively, as the volume fraction of the Al 11(Ce,Y)3 phase increased from 10.45 to 19.15%.
